newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goldfields shares jump on Placer bids.
newsitem.headline: Goldfields shares jump on Placer bids.

text.p: Shares of Goldfields Ltd, part owner of the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea, rose 19 cents or 7.7 percent to A$2.65 in early trade on Thursday after Placer Dome Inc's bid for Highlands Gold Ltd.

"The market is saying if Placer Dome is prepared to pay A$2.00 for Placer Pacific and 75 cents for Highlands then there must be more to Porgera than meets the eye," said Bell Commodities gold analyst Keith Goode.
Placer Dome earlier launched a 75 cents a share bid for Highlands and an offer to mop up the 24.6 percent of its Australian offshoot Placer Pacific that it does not already own.
Highlands, Placer Pacific, Goldfields and the Papua New Guinea government own equal shares in the one million ounce a year Porgera mine in the Papua New Guinea Highlands.
Shares in another large Papua New Guinea gold project, Lihir Gold Ltd, were also stronger, up 18 cents or 7.8 percent to A$2.49.

Goode said the gold sector appeared to have been bolstered by recent exploration results in the Gawler Craton in South Australia, and a perception that Australian stocks were cheap by international standards.
